source.raw_text:
SYNOPSIS

Title
Visual and Patient-Reported Outcomes after Mix-and-Match Implantation of an Extended Depth of Focus and a Trifocal Intraocular Lens

What type of request are you submitting?
Formal Study Proposal (detailed study design)

Are you the Principal Investigator?
No 

Region(s) where your study will be located: (select all that apply)
Americas

Study Type
Investigator Initiated Study

Describe Hypothesis
The hypothesis is that mix-and-match implantation of the PureSee and Odyssey intraocular lenses (IOLs) will result in excellent visual outcomes at distance, intermediate, and near, high patient satisfaction, and low reports of visual disturbances. 


For analytical purposes, is this a bilateral or unilateral study?
Bilateral

Total Sample Size
Treatment: 40 subjects
Control:0

Sample Size Justification
We estimate that 35 subjects will be sufficient to characterize the performance of the mix-and-match approach using PureSee and Odyssey. To account for dropout, the sample size will be increased to 40. 
1. Hacopian AG, Brunson PB, Hall B. Patient Reported Outcomes and Visual Acuity After Bilateral Implantation of a Next Generation Presbyopia Correcting Intraocular Lens. OPTH. 2026;20:1-8. doi:10.2147/OPTH.S572703

Please list all the patient visits (e.g. pre-op, post-op 3 months, etc.) as required for the study
    • Preoperative (Screening)
    • Operative (one visit per eye)
    • 3 Month postoperative

Study Status
Fully developed protocol: No
IRB: Not submitted

Study Synopsis
Observational, Prospective, None

Study Duration
Enrollment: 6M
Follow-Up: 3M
Data Analysis: 1M

Describe Study Objectives and Significance
The TECNIS Odyssey is a new full range of vision IOL, with current reports suggests high visual acuity and spectacle independence at distance, intermediate, and near.1,2

The TECNIS PureSee is a new non-diffractive extended depth of focus (EDOF) IOL. The non-diffractive design may reduce reports of dysphotopsias and improve contrast sensitivity compared to diffractive IOLs. A large randomized control trial suggesting better intermediate and near vision with the PureSee IOL, compared to a monofocal control, and similar contrast sensitivity, distance vision, and dysphotopsia profile.3

Mix-and-match implantation of an EDOF IOL in the dominant eye and multifocal IOL in the non-dominant eye may enable better range of vision and fewer visual disturbances compared to bilateral implantation of the EDOF or trifocal IOLs alone.
To date there are minimal data on visual outcomes, patient satisfaction, and patient-reported dysphotopsias using mix-and-match implantation of the PureSee (dominant eye) and the Odyssey (non-dominant eye).

The objective of this study is to test the hypothesis that mix-and-match implantation of the PureSee and Odyssey IOLs will result in excellent visual outcomes at distance, intermediate, and near, high patient satisfaction, and low reports of visual disturbances.

The objective will be completed by a prospective, observational study of 3 month postoperative binocular uncorrected and distance-corrected visual acuities at distance (UDVA, CDVA), intermediate (UIVA, DCIVA; 66 cm), and near (UNVA, DCNVA; 40 cm), binocular distance-corrected defocus curve, and administration of the Assessment of IntraOcular Lens Implant Symptoms (AIOLIS) questionnaire. 

1. Hacopian AG, Brunson PB, Hall B. Patient Reported Outcomes and Visual Acuity After Bilateral Implantation of a Next Generation Presbyopia Correcting Intraocular Lens. OPTH. 2026;20:1-8. doi:10.2147/OPTH.S572703
2. Bissen-Miyajima H, Midorikawa M, Fujisaki R, Ota Y, Minami K, Honda R. Early Clinical Results of a Newly Developed Continuous Range of Vision Intraocular Lens. Ophthalmol Ther. 2025;14(11):2937-2945. doi:10.1007/s40123-025-01235-7
3.  Corbett D, Black D, Roberts TV, Cronin B, Gunn D, Bala C, Versace P, Tsai L, Papadatou E, Alarcon A, Vilupuru S. Quality of vision clinical outcomes for a new fully-refractive extended depth of focus Intraocular Lens. Eye. 2024;38(S1):9-14. doi:10.1038/s41433-024-03039-8

Primary Endpoint
- Binocular DCIVA (66 cm)

Secondary Endpoints
    • Mean binocular CDVA
    • Mean binocular UIVA (66 cm)
    • Mean binocular UDVA
    • Mean binocular DCNVA (40 cm)
    • Mean binocular UNVA (40cm)
    • Binocular distance-corrected defocus curve (+1.0 D through -2.50 D)
    • Percentages of subject responses on each of the AIOLIS questionnaire questions. 

Inclusion Criteria
    • Adult patients undergoing age-related cataract surgery.

Exclusion Criteria
    • Moderate-severe any disease state (deemed by the surgeon) that could increase risk of complicated cataract surgery (ie, pseudoexfoliation syndrome, zonular dehiscence, history of eye trauma, and prior refractive surgery)

Control Arm
None

One cohort and no control arm; the synopsis describes no research treatment assignment or randomization.

procedures.assessments: Screening: informed consent, demographics and medical history. One operative visit per eye. At 3 months postoperative, binocular uncorrected and distance-corrected photopic visual acuity at distance, 66 cm intermediate and 40 cm near, binocular distance-corrected defocus curve (+1.0 D through -2.50 D), AIOLIS questionnaire, monitoring of adverse events and device deficiencies, and exit form completion.
procedures.methods: At 3 months postoperative measure binocular uncorrected and distance-corrected photopic acuities at distance (UDVA, CDVA), intermediate 66 cm (UIVA, DCIVA), and near 40 cm (UNVA, DCNVA). Obtain binocular distance-corrected defocus curve from +1.0 D through -2.50 D, and administer AIOLIS, reporting percentages for each question. No defocus step interval, acuity chart/unit/distance for distance testing, questionnaire response anchors or score conversion is supplied.

assessment_details.operative_occurrences: One operative visit per eye; two operative encounters for each bilaterally treated participant.
assessment_details.exit_form: The synopsis says Complete Exit Form1 at Month 3; normalize the activity name to Complete exit form without inventing footnote content.

statistics.analysis_plan: At 3 months postoperative, binocular visual acuity measurements and the distance-corrected defocus curve will be summarized using the number of observations, mean, standard deviation, median, minimum and maximum. AIOLIS responses will be summarized for each question using counts and percentages. Where baseline and follow-up measurements exist, observed changes from baseline will be summarized descriptively. Use available observations and report each denominator; missing values will not be imputed. Results are descriptive; no inferential hypothesis tests, power claims or multiplicity adjustments are planned.

safety.monitoring: Monitor adverse events and device deficiencies at the 3-month postoperative assessment.
